Two new 5k+ hits, both personal numbers stories from the same author. The renter vent is plateauing at 44.7k, and renter-to-owner posts are rising. Nothing new from the watchlist to score.
narrative_synthesis: The meta is shifting from rent anxiety to 'how do I stop renting', told through real numbers. Drafts: (1) a first-deal numbers story Bar fills with his own real figures, (2) a renter-to-owner take, (3) a Philly zoning question.

drafts.draft_en:
My first deal, in real numbers:

Bought for [$___]
Put down [$___]
Rehab [$___]
Rents for [$___]/mo
What I'd do differently: [one line]

Nobody starts with a perfect deal. You start with one that pays you.
drafts.pattern: personal numbers story (Jacob_Naviaux 6.5k and 5.7k, two hits in a day). Fill the brackets with your own real figures only; don't post with placeholders.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 20-30s, numbers on screen one line at a time as you say them. Film in front of the property if you can.

drafts.draft_en:
A lot of renters are closer to owning than they think.

The bank isn't the only door. Some sellers will carry the financing themselves if the terms make sense for both sides.

If you're renting in Philly and want to own, start by asking the question.
drafts.pattern: renter-to-owner angle (REIMakayla 'tenants with better credit' 1.6k, mikepat711 'first-time buying is confusing' 2.6k) + seller financing
drafts.video_tip: Selfie walk on a Philly block, 15-20s. Hook in the first 2 seconds: 'Renting and think you can't buy?' No promises about approval, rates or timelines.

drafts.draft_en:
If Pennsylvania loosens zoning, what are you building on a Philly lot first?

Duplex?
Triplex?
Backyard unit?

More housing is coming one way or another. I'd rather be ready than surprised.
